newsitem.title: USA: Colgate sales up 5 pct, slowed by currency.
newsitem.headline: Colgate sales up 5 pct, slowed by currency.

text.p: Colgate-Palmolive Co said on Wednesday its first quarter sales were up five percent to $2.1 billion, and would have risen almost eight percent if not for currency translation.

Colgate said its North American sales were up seven percent on eight percent unit volume growth, while Latin American sales rose 10 percent on eight percent unit volume growth, boosted by stronger worldwide advertising.

"The simultaneous increase in both advertising and profitability was made possible by a sharp increase in gross profit together with a reduction in the worldwide overhead ratio," Colgate Chairman Reuben Mark said in a statement.
In Europe the company had two percent higher unit volume, but sales declined six percent, reflecting the impact of currency translation, Colgate said.
In its Asia/Africa unit, sales increased three percent, on four percent unit volume growth, with strong advances in India, China, Taiwan and Australia offset by the Philippines and Thailand.
Hill's Pet Nutrition sales were up 23 percent, on unit volume growth of 19 percent, the company said.
